05-045.r: Correct: Buddha's mother → Koliyan princess; Parshvanatha (twenty-third Tirthankara) → Banaras. Wrong: Mahavira's mother Trishala was Chetaka's sister, not his daughter.
05-045.t: Trishala = Chetaka's sister; Chellana (Bimbisara's wife) = Chetaka's daughter.

05-046.r: Correct: Kalinga king Kharavela patronised Jainism (first century BC). Bhadrabahu (not Sthulabhadra) spread Jainism in South India; his followers → Digambaras.

05-047.r: Jain doctrine: every object, even the smallest particle, has a soul; karma is the bane of the soul and must end; penance destroys karma → all three.

05-048.r: Samadhi Maran (Sallekhana, Sanyasna Maran) → Jain last vow: gradually giving up food and liquid at life's end.

05-049.r: Ikshvakus of South India (3rd-4th century) followed Vedic religion but supported Buddhism → statement 1 wrong; Palas of Bengal patronised Buddhism → 2 correct.

05-050.r: Ajivika sect → founded (popularised) by Makkhali Gosala, an early disciple of Mahavira; belief 'Niyativad': fate decides everything, man is helpless.

05-054.r: Ajivikas → believed in determinism (fate) and austerity; the order of rebirth cannot be changed → 1 and 3 correct.

05-055.r: Ajivikas → nude wandering ascetics who begged in towns and lived in rock-cut caves (Barabar), not forest dwellers; respected in the Maurya era → only II.

05-056.r: Ajivikas: Makkhali Gosala the chief leader; central idea Niyati (fate); held regular sabhas; they rejected caste discrimination (C wrong) → A, B, D.

05-057.r: Souls exist also in rocks, running water and other natural objects (soul in every particle) → Jainism.

05-058.r: Lakulisa → Pashupata; Nagarjuna → Sunyavada; Bhadrabahu → Jain; Gosala → Ajivika.

05-059.r: Barabar caves → shelters for Ajivikas, cut under Ashoka and his grandson Dasaratha (also Nagarjuni hills).

05-060.r: Kaushambi (U.P.) → pilgrimage for both Buddhists and Jains; Nicakshu shifted the capital there from flood-hit Hastinapur.

05-061.r: Wrong: Gomateshwara (Sravanabelagola) is Bahubali, son of first Tirthankara Rishabhnath, not the last Tirthankara. True: Tawang has India's largest monastery; Khajuraho by Chandelas.

05-062.r: Gommateshwara (Bahubali) statue at Sravanabelagola → built by Chamundraya, minister of Ganga ruler Rachmalla-IV, about 981 A.D.

05-063.r: Mahamastakabhisheka → Bahubali (Gomateshwara) statue at Shravanabelagola, Karnataka; held every twelve years; statue 18 metres high.

06-001.r: Four yugas in order → Krita, Treta, Dvapara, Kali.

06-002.r: Mattamayura → Shaiva sect of ancient India, known from Chedi dynasty inscriptions.

06-003.r: Ardhanarishvara (half Shiva, half Parvati) → union of God with his Shakti (masculine and feminine energies).

06-004.r: Nayanars → Tamil devotees of Shiva (Shaiva); Alvars → Tamil devotees of Vishnu.

06-006.r: Not an Alvar saint → Tirugyan. Alvars: Poigai, Pudam, Thirumangai.

06-007.r: Only woman among the 12 Alvar saints (Vaishnavism, Tamil Nadu) → Andal.

06-008.r: Bhagavata (Vaishnava) religion peaked under the Guptas: state religion; kings titled 'Parambhagavata'; Garuda (Vishnu's mount) was the state symbol.

06-009.r: Originator of Bhagavata religion → Krishna (Vasudeva, Vrishni/Satvat clan, Mathura); Chhandogya Upanishad calls him son of Devaki, disciple of Ghor Angirasa.

06-011.r: First worshippers of Vasudeva Krishna → Bhagavatas (called Vasudevak in Panini's age).

06-012.r: Deity shown holding a plough → Balarama (Haldhar), Krishna's brother.

06-013.r: Forms of bhakti in the Bhagavata cult → 9 (Navadha Bhakti), for attaining Moksha.

06-014.r: Heliodorus' Garuda pillar, Besnagar (Vidisha) → only Vasudeva ('Devadeva'); earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavatism; Heliodorus was a Yavana envoy from Taxila.

06-018.r: Vishnu's incarnation saving the Earth from the sea → Varaha; killed demon Hiranyaksha and rose from the sea balancing Earth on his teeth.

06-019.r: Astika vs Nastika systems → belief in the authority of the Vedas (Astika accept it, Nastika reject it).

06-020.r: Equal weight to Jnana, Karma and Bhakti for liberation → Bhagavad Gita. Advaita (Shankara) → Brahma the only truth; Mimamsa → only Karma.

06-021.r: Main teaching of the Gita → Nishkama Karma Yoga (acting unselfishly, without expecting reward).

06-022.r: 'Ananga' (incorporeal) → Kama (Kamadeva), god of love; wife Rati; other names Kandarpa, Madana, Manmatha.

06-023.r: Prasthanatrayi of Vedanta → Upanishads, Brahmasutra, Bhagavad Gita; Bhagavata is not included.

06-024.r: Mahabharata narrated before 60,000 hermits → Naimisharanya (Sitapur, U.P.), by Sut Goswami to Saunak; earlier Vaisampayana told it to Janamejaya.

06-025.r: First meeting of Rama and Hanuman → Kishkindha Kand (fourth of seven Kands of Valmiki's Ramayana); also Bali's death, Sugriva crowned.

06-026.r: Kalika Purana (Kali/Sati Purana) → Shaktism upapurana, likely composed in Assam; attributed to sage Markandeya.

06-027.r: Shiva → trident; Vishnu → chakra; Ganesh → rope or noose; Saraswati → veena.

06-028.r: Rathyatra at Puri (Odisha), Ashadha Shukla Paksha → Lord Jagannath (Krishna) with Balbhadra and Subhadra.

06-029.r: Kumbh Mela, every twelve years: Nasik → Godavari; Haridwar → Ganga; Prayag → Ganga-Yamuna confluence; Ujjain → Kshipra.

06-030.r: Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis → made devotional religion popular in Northern India; criticised rituals and social order; urged renunciation.

06-031.r: Holy places: Jainism → Pavapuri; Hinduism → Varanasi; Islam → Medina; Christianity → Vatican.

07-001.r: Earliest extant coins of India → silver punch-marked (Aahat) coins.

07-002.r: Wrong pair: Koshala's capitals were Saket and Shravasti, not Ahichchhatra. Correct: Anga-Champa, Vatsa-Kaushambi, Matsya-Viratnagar.

07-003.r: Pradyot → Avanti; Udayan → Vatsa; Prasenjit → Koshala; Ajatshatru → Magadha.

07-004.r: Chand Pradyota → ruler of Avanti (Ujjain); contemporary of Buddha and Bimbisara; Bimbisara sent physician Jivak to treat his jaundice.

07-005.r: Canal dug under a Nanda king (Mahapadmananda) → Kalinga; known from the Hathigumpha inscription.

07-006.r: Ancient name of Ujjain (Malwa) → Avantika; one of the two capitals of Avanti, one of the 16 Mahajanapadas.

07-007.r: Map of Mahajanapadas A-D → Matsya (capital Viratnagar, Rajasthan), Avanti (Ujjayini, Mahishmati), Vatsa (Prayagraj-Kaushambi), Anga.

07-008.r: City named in both Mahabharata and Mahabhashya → Madhyamika (Nagari) and Viratnagar (Bairat; capital of Matsya, founded by King Virat).
07-008.c: No answer printed; two options (Madhyamika, Viratnagar) fit.

07-009.r: Ajatashatru (Bimbisara's successor) fortified Pataligrama; his successor Udayin founded the city of Pataliputra and shifted Magadha's capital there from Rajgriha.
07-009.c: Ajatashatru only fortified Pataligrama; Udayin is usually credited with founding the city of Pataliputra and moving the capital there, so (a) Udayin is the standard answer.

07-010.r: Ancient Pataliputra (Patna) → Ganga to the north, Son to the west.

07-011.r: Pataliputra: founded by Ajatashatru (Haryanka); Udayin first made it capital; among these options → Chandragupta Maurya.
07-011.t: Udayin is the true first; choose Chandragupta Maurya only if Udayin is absent.

07-014.r: Area south of the Ganga in ancient times → Magadha (so 'none of the above'); Takshashila → between Indus and Jhelum.

07-015.r: Udayan-Vasavadatta legend → Ujjain; Bhasa's drama 'Svapnavasavadattam': Vatsa king Udayan and Vasavadatta, daughter of Avanti king Pradyot.

07-016.r: First Magadhan empire → sixth century B.C.; founder Bimbisara (about 544-492 B.C.) of the Haryanka dynasty.
